Point the camera at what you want to know about, then use the Ask button to ask a question — for example \"what colour is this?\" Sight Buddy captures the picture as you finish and answers. Ask nothing to simply hear the scene described.\n\nAfter that, use Ask again to ask more about the same picture, or tap Capture for a fresh description.

With Live text on (in More or in settings; off at first) and Preview on, text in view is shown over the camera where it sits, to read with TalkBack or to select and copy, and read out once when new text comes into view. Tap a box to pin it and hear it, to copy from; the rest stays live. Tap outside the boxes to let it go.

To read a page in full, tap Capture: it says looking for text, then guides you to the text, saying no text visible until it sees some, then left, right, up or down to bring the page to the middle of the view, and closer or further when the text is too small or runs off both sides. When it says hold steady, keep still for two seconds and it takes the picture and reads the page, section by section. Tap Capture again while it is guiding to take the picture straight away.

You can also use Ask, or type, to ask a question about the text. Asked before any page is captured, it guides you to the text first, the same way, and answers once the picture is taken.

To take pictures yourself instead, turn off Guidance, in More or in settings: Capture then takes the picture at once.
Move the camera slowly. Sight Buddy names the most confident object it sees, with a short pause between announcements so speech stays clear.
Use the Ask button and say what to find, for example \"keys\" or \"cup\". The voice guides you: left, right, up, down, or centred. Tap Objects to pick from a list.
Point the camera at the scene. Sight Buddy reports whether lighting is bright, dim, or dark based on the camera image.
Point the camera so the colour fills the small frame in the centre of the screen. Sight Buddy speaks the colour name. Works best in good, even lighting — dim or warm indoor light can shift colours.

Along the top, left to right: Help opens this help. Memories lists the chats you have saved. More opens a second row of buttons: Save chat in the chat features, Torch for the phone\'s light, Preview, then this feature\'s own switches. Settings opens settings. Preview shows the camera behind the screen; any messages stay, faint, over it.

Swipe with two fingers to change feature. The feature bar along the bottom lists every feature; tap one to go straight there.
With looping off, the first and last features say when there is no feature further that way.
Mute silences this feature\'s voice until you leave it; Unmute brings it back. To have features start muted, turn on Start features muted in settings.

Capture takes a picture and describes it. Ask: tap, speak your question, then tap Send. Or type a question in the box above the buttons and tap Send.

Everything said in this session is shown above as messages you can read, select and copy. Leaving the feature starts it over.

While an answer is on its way, a soft tick plays.

In More, Auto capture takes the picture for you when you press Ask with no picture yet; off, press Capture first.

Capture starts guiding you to the text, then takes the picture; tap it again to take the picture at once. Ask: tap, speak your question about the text, then tap Send. Or type a question in the box above the buttons and tap Send.

The text and the answers are shown above as messages you can read, select and copy. Leaving the feature starts it over.

While an answer is on its way, a soft tick plays.

In More: Guidance guides you to the text before the picture is taken. Summarize has the AI sum up the captured text instead of reading it all first. Live text shows the text in view over the camera.

Objects opens the list of objects to choose from. Ask: tap, say what to find, then tap Send. Or type an object in the box and tap Send. What you asked for and the replies are shown above.\n\nIn More, Pitch swaps the spoken directions for a held note that rises as the object nears the middle of the view.

Do you want to use OpenAI speech recognition for the best user experience? This will enhance the user experience, but will add a minor API cost, about a fraction of a penny per minute of recording time. If enabled, the recorded audio is sent to OpenAI for processing instead of being processed by the system engine. Recommended for users who do not have the voice enhancement models downloaded.
